content.title: Standard Equation of a Circle
content.overview: The standard form of a circle's equation allows for the immediate identification of its center and radius. This lesson covers how to interpret the standard form and how to convert general quadratic equations into standard form using the 'completing the square' method.
learning_objectives: Identify the center (h, k) and radius r from the standard equation of a circle.
Convert a general form circle equation into standard form by completing the square.
Apply the relationship between the signs in the equation and the coordinates of the center.

sections.title: The Standard Form Equation
sections.content:
The standard form of a circle equation is (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r², where (h, k) represents the coordinates of the center and r represents the radius. Note the subtraction signs in the formula: a term like (x - 3) indicates an x-coordinate of +3, while (x + 3) indicates an x-coordinate of -3. The value on the right side of the equation is the square of the radius (r²), not the radius itself.

![A circle centered at (2, -3) with a radius of 5 units.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/6f64bba7-bc12-48ba-8c95-930696bb5aeb-1786506032198-969.webp)

sections.title: Converting from General Form
sections.content: When an equation is given in general form (x² + y² + Ax + By + C = 0), you must use the 'Group-and-Complete' strategy. First, group the x-terms together and the y-terms together, moving the constant C to the other side of the equals sign. Second, complete the square for each group by adding (coefficient/2)² to both sides of the equation. Finally, factor the trinomials into squared binomials to reach the standard form.

worked_examples.question: Convert the equation x² + y² - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0 into standard form and identify the center and radius.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Group the x and y terms and move the constant: (x² - 4x) + (y² + 6y) = 12. Step 2: Complete the square for x. Take half of -4 (-2) and square it (4). Add 4 to both sides. Step 3: Complete the square for y. Take half of 6 (3) and square it (9). Add 9 to both sides. The equation becomes: (x² - 4x + 4) + (y² + 6y + 9) = 12 + 4 + 9. Step 4: Factor into binomial squares: (x - 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25. Step 5: Identify components. The center (h, k) is (2, -3) and the radius r is √25 = 5.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the radius or forgetting to take the square root of the constant to find the radius.
Sign errors when identifying the center: (x - h) means the coordinate is h, but (x + h) means the coordinate is -h.
Adding the 'completing the square' constants to only one side of the equation instead of both.
exam_tips: If you are stuck on a multiple-choice question, you can expand the answer choices to see which one matches the original general form equation.
Always check if the x² and y² coefficients are 1 before completing the square; if they aren't, divide the entire equation by that coefficient first.
The radius must always be a positive value; if your r² is negative, re-check your arithmetic.
content.recap: The standard equation (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² defines a circle with center (h, k) and radius r. Use completing the square to transform general equations into this form, ensuring you balance both sides of the equation.

knowledge_claims.content: The standard form of a circle equation is (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r².
In the standard circle equation, the point (h, k) represents the center of the circle.
In the standard circle equation, the constant on the right side represents the square of the radius (r²).
To find the radius r from the standard equation, you must take the square root of the constant on the right side.
A term written as (x + h)² in the standard equation indicates that the x-coordinate of the center is -h.
A term written as (x - h)² in the standard equation indicates that the x-coordinate of the center is +h.
The first step in converting a general circle equation to standard form is grouping x-terms and y-terms and moving the constant to the opposite side.
To complete the square for a quadratic expression x² + Ax, you must add the constant (A/2)².
When completing the square, any constant added to the left side of the equation must also be added to the right side to maintain equality.
A common error is failing to change the sign of h or k when extracting the center coordinates from the binomial squares.
If the coefficients of x² and y² are not 1, you must divide the entire equation by that coefficient before completing the square.
A circle equation where r² = 0 represents a single point (the center), not a circle with area.
After completing the square, the expression x² + Ax + (A/2)² factors into the perfect square binomial (x + A/2)².
You can verify a standard form conversion by expanding the binomials to see if they return the original linear terms and constant.

Which equation is a circle centered at (2,-3) with radius 3?
A) (x+2)²+(y-3)²=9
B) (x-2)²+(y+3)²=3
C) (x-2)²+(y+3)²=9
D) y=(x-2)²-3

Practice form 2.
Which equation is a circle centered at (3,-4) with radius 4?
A) (x-3)²+(y+4)²=16
B) (x+3)²+(y-4)²=16
C) (x-3)²+(y+4)²=4
D) y=(x-3)²-4

videoLesson.title: Complete Squares to Standardize a Circle
videoLesson.description: Recognize center and radius from x and y variable groups and constants. Group x and y terms, complete squares, then isolate constants to read (h,k) and r.
